'''Banchob Sripa''' ({{langx|th|บรรจบ ศรีภา}}, {{RTGS|Banchop Sipa}}; born 4 December 1958) is a Thai scientist who is professor and Director of the Tropical Disease Research Center (TDRC) at [[Khon Kaen University]] in [[Khon Kaen]], Thailand. He is also the head of the World Health Organization Collaborating Centre for Research and Control of [[Opisthorchiasis]], an infectious parasitic disease caused by the [[Opisthorchis viverrini|Southeast Asian liver fluke]], which is endemic in [[Isan|northeastern Thailand]] and other portions of the [[Mekong River]] basin. He is also coordinator for the [[neglected tropical diseases|Asian Neglected Tropical Disease Network]]. He has a doctorate in tropical health from the [[University of Queensland]], Australia. He received the Outstanding Scientist Award from the Foundation for the Promotion of Science and Technology in 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=รศ.ดร.บรรจบ ศรีภาผู้บุกเบิกวิจัยกลไกโรคพยาธิใบไม้ตับเชิงลึก|url=http://www.manager.co.th/science/ViewNews.aspx?NewsID=9560000096245|accessdate=6 March 2018|work=Manager Online|date=4 August 2013|language=th}}</ref>

==The Lawa model==
An [[The Integrated Opisthorchiasis Control Program|opisthorchiasis control program]] known as the "Lawa model" was started in 2007 by the Tropical Disease Research Laboratory (TDRL) under Banchob. Using an [[EcoHealth]] approach, the program has been more successful than earlier control programs. The program operates in 12 villages surrounding the Lawa Lake south of Khon Kaen. The liver fluke infection rate has declined to less than 10 percent from an average of 60 percent since the start of the program.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Sripa|first1=B|last2=Tangkawattana|first2=S|last3=Sangnikul|first3=T|title=The Lawa model: A sustainable, integrated opisthorchiasis control program using the EcoHealth approach in the Lawa Lake region of Thailand.|journal=Parasitology International|date=August 2017|volume=66|issue=4|pages=346–354|doi=10.1016/j.parint.2016.11.013|pmid=27890720|pmc=5443708}}</ref> Banchob has published more than 200 peer-reviewed scientific articles and eight book chapters in English.
